cp06_false_premise.finding: Unwarranted abstention on false premises is not gated: a system that is perfect except that it abstains on every frozen false-premise record stays eligible (over-abstention 0.044 <= 0.10). Report over-abstention by case type before trusting a winner.

cp07_bilingual.agent_reading: Read every distinct held-out unit (EN statement against statement_zh): no meaning drift found. statement_zh is a translation of statement, so an EN/ZH pair is one claim: a wrong rule is wrong in both languages and their agreement confirms nothing.
cp07_bilingual.finding: decision.py counts human-judged EXAMPLES (>= 100), but the frozen evaluation's 180 unit records cover only 45 objectives; the same corrected sentence recurs in single and two-error records and many objectives are asked in French, Chinese and English. Translations and reused sentences are not independent evidence: report human F1 by objective (or with a cluster bootstrap) and never count the frozen and rb outputs of one learner text as two examples.

findings: Degenerate outputs `null`, `{}` and `{"units": null}` are accepted by the production parser as zero units and counted valid_empty, i.e. as a correct abstention on a zero reference; the strict knowledge_extraction_v2 schema forbids them, and strict_schema_findings already reports them (top_level_not_object / units_not_list) but account() only demotes extra/missing-key findings.

A non-string output_text aborts the whole comparison (the Go validator refuses the line) instead of being one invalid row; a raw row without output_text and a cut last line also abort it. These fail loudly (no silent miscount) and predict.py writes neither, but a partial file from a stopped job needs its last line removed by hand.

cp12_denominators.paired_invalid_never_consistent: paired.report: invalid or missing -> not consistent, not correct

f1_denominator_probe.system: oracle except 9 frozen references with the most units truncated at max_new_tokens

cp12_denominators.finding: Structural validity, abstention, over-abstention and the paired metrics count every reference row (an invalid, truncated, extra-key or missing row counts against the system). Unit F1 does not: quality.report computes precision and recall over valid outputs only, so the reference units of truncated or malformed rows leave the recall denominator. The same holds for human F1 built with `quality --judgments`. The 0.98 validity gate bounds the effect (at most 9 of 472 rows), but those rows can be the hardest ones, and the 0.05 win margin is decided on that F1.
